analysis:
The PR only changes documentation: docs/provider/cli-reference.md and docs/reference/protocol-messages.md. It adds a new drain semantic for the no-registered-session case and a coordinator handshake deadline row. I found no source or control change.

Drain: docs/provider/cli-reference.md (head ~444-448) and docs/reference/protocol-messages.md (head 170-174) say a lifecycle drain completes without the coordinator acknowledgement only when no work is left and no coordinator session is registered, for example during a reconnect. A registered session must still acknowledge before the deadline. The text keeps the earlier statement that a barrier may have fenced the old session and that admission stays closed until a confirmed drain and reconnect. This is consistent with T-053-style stale-session concerns and TB-002. It is a documentation claim about ProviderLoop+Lifecycle.swift `performLifecycleDrain`, and that code was not supplied, so I could not check it. The residual question for a deeper pass is whether the implementation really cannot skip the ack for a session that is registered but momentarily stale. This is an unverified contract, not a finding.

Handshake: the new row (head line 1974) documents a 30 s deadline for TCP, TLS and WebSocket upgrade, with cancel and retry under backoff. That is an availability hardening on the provider-to-coordinator boundary (TB-002). It cannot be checked because CoordinatorConnectionHandshake.swift was not supplied.

Remaining content in the viewed ranges (the models location, benchmark, logout/unenroll, report, env passthrough and the cache sections) appears to be unchanged context. It is consistent with T-041 (SSD cache), the A-008 logout notes and TB-011 (App Attest). No threat-model assumption looks invalidated and no new attack surface is evident. The threat model may want a note about no-session drain completion if the implementation changes the drain guarantees.
